name: Helen Landó Helman
role: The survivor at the centre of the project; the researcher's grandmother

birthRecord.note: Registered under mother's surname Landó; father named only in the remarks. No surname entered for the child.

fate: Only survivor of her immediate family; mother, father and five siblings murdered. Sent to Budapest late 1943, then through DP camps to the USA on the SS Marine Marlin, May 1947.

photos.caption: Indersdorf, Germany, with her best friend Ibi Weinberger
With Sam, Huntington Beach High School graduation

name: Zacharias Helman
arrest: Recorded 15 May 1944 at Tiszabogdány (conflicts with district roundup date)

body: Born 1901 in Tiszabogdány. A carter. Married to Roza Landó, six children.
Auschwitz 26 May. Buchenwald 2 June. Magdeburg-Rothensee on 23 July.
Worked past use, he was ordered back to Auschwitz that October.
faceCard.fate: Murdered at Auschwitz, about 10 October 1944, on the ground where his wife and children had waited five months before.

name: Lajos Helman
fate: Survived. Liberated at Terezín, 8 May 1945. In Budapest June 1945 (registered 8 June) he and Michal found Helen.

faceCard.who: Helen's first cousin. Nineteen years old.
body: Born 9 December 1924 in Tiszabogdány. A carter, like his uncle.
Arrested 10 April 1944, five weeks before the others on this card.
Auschwitz 24 May. Buchenwald 2 June. Sent on to the synthetic-fuel plant at Rehmsdorf.

name: Michal Helman
fate: Survived. Liberated at Terezín, 8 May 1945. In Budapest June 1945 he and Lajos found Helen and told her what had happened to her family.

faceCard.who: Helen's first cousin. Eighteen years old.
body: Born 15 October 1925 in Tiszabogdány. A carter.
Auschwitz 26 May. Buchenwald 2 June. Rehmsdorf, then the evacuation and the march.
At Terezín he was billeted in block C III/257.
faceCard.fate: Survived. In Budapest in June 1945 he and Lajos found Helen and told her what had happened to her family.

name: Roza Landó
fate: Murdered on arrival at Auschwitz with five of the children, 26 May 1944.

name: Iczik Helman
note: Did not understand Hungarian; entries read to him in a language he understood. Signed in his own hand.

name: David Helman

birthRecord.citation: Fund 1606, Opus 9, Delo 155 · scan from Sub-Carpathia Genealogy

fate: Fled east into the Soviet Union in 1939, joined the Red Army, and fell at Stalingrad about 1943 (Soviet side of the front).

name: Miksa Helman
role: Iczik's son; father of Lajos and Michal; Zacharias's brother
note: Placed in Iczik's household by the 1921 Czechoslovak census. Never reached Buchenwald; stayed at Auschwitz. Absent from the 1,000-name roll under any surname.

name: Adél Petranker
role: Miksa's wife; mother of Lajos and Michal
note: Named on Yad Vashem Pages of Testimony filed by surviving children from Israel in the 1990s.

name: Jenő Helman
fate: Taken with his son Mordekhai to the Fünfteichen subcamp; died there about January 1945.

name: Hermina (Hinda) Helman
role: Eldest of Zacharias and Roza's six children; Helen's sibling

birthRecord.note: Mother entered under maiden name Landó; father Zigmund Helman in the remarks only.
birthRecord.citation: Fund 1606, Opus 9 · scan from Sub-Carpathia Genealogy

name: Samantha Seligman-Grajewski
role: Founder of Engineering Remembrance; the researcher (3G, granddaughter of Helen)
bio: Process engineer finishing an M.S. in Chemical Engineering at Stanford. Began the research in 2026 with no prior training in Holocaust research or genealogy.

name: Tibor (Tibi) Katz
role: Helen's husband; from the family she married into
origin: Szatmár / Satu Mare, Transylvania (4 Kossuth Lajos utca)
fate: Survived a death march out of Budapest under the Arrow Cross (feigned death and escaped). DP camp at Ainring, then Palestine. Married Helen in Los Angeles in the 1960s.

name: Eva Katz
fate: Seized with her mother Margit leaving home; forced onto the death march west, then deported to Bergen-Belsen, where she survived as a small child.
